models_evaluated: ResNet CNN polyp classifier with GradCAM (intrinsic) and SHAP via Captum (extrinsic) explanations

links.outcome: Physician preference and perceived understanding/trust for intrinsic (GradCAM) versus extrinsic (SHAP) visual explanations
links.effect: Intrinsic explanations preferred (30 of 47 multiple-choice respondents chose intrinsic as useful; 14 wanted both; 3 extrinsic). Extrinsic described as confusing. Fleiss kappa 0.049 (poor agreement on preferred method).
links.quote: Our results show that intrinsic explanations are preferred.

links.outcome: Whether physicians' judgments of saliency explanations reflect understanding versus expectation of lesion alignment
links.effect: Preference for the intrinsic method may be superficial rather than reflect understanding of what the explanations convey; explanations aligned with the lesion may be favored, risking unwarranted judgments and misplaced trust.
links.quote: However, the free-form responses in our survey strongly suggest that the underlying reason for the doctors’ preference for this method may be more superficial than actually understanding what information the different explanations convey.

unlisted_practices: Comparing intrinsic (GradCAM) versus extrinsic (SHAP) saliency explanation formats for clinician preference
Providing clinicians an introduction/training on explanation methods before use

openai.country: International; participants came from eight countries

links.effect: 30 chose intrinsic explanations, 14 chose both explanation methods, and 3 chose extrinsic explanations as useful in clinical practice.
links.quote: From Fig 5c , we see that 30 participants answered that the intrinsic explanation method would be useful in clinical practice, 14 participants wanted both explanation methods, while 3 wanted the extrinsic explanation method.

links.effect: Extrinsic explanations were described by several participants as complicated, confusing, hard to interpret, hard to understand, unnatural, and harder to grasp.
links.quote: Based on similar free-form answers from several participants, describing Method B as “complicated”, “confusing”, “hard to interpret”, “hard to understand”, “doesn’t feel natural”, and “harder to grasp visually”, we conclude that the extrinsic explanations functionality of highlighting in which direction each collection of image pixels drives the prediction is counterintuitive to domain experts not familiar with such a way to represent information.

links.outcome: inter-rater agreement on AI explanation methods
links.effect: Fleiss' kappa was 0.049 (95% CI, 0.033 to 0.066, p < 0.001), indicating poor agreement among participants on preferred explanation methods.
links.quote: The results, as detailed in Table 3 , show a Fleiss’ kappa value of 0.049.
